intro.title: Network security
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple network security simulator that demonstrates how firewalls filter incoming connections. You will learn to implement basic packet filtering logic by checking connection requests against security rules. The core programming concept involves using conditional statements to make security decisions based on source and destination data. You will work with fundamental security constructs like allow/deny rules and port validation. This hands-on exercise will help you understand how network security controls traffic flow in real-world systems.
intro.usecase: Network security principles are foundational to every web application that handles user data or sensitive operations. Developers implement these concepts when building secure login forms, encrypted payment dashboards, and admin panels that require authentication and authorization. For example, a banking app's transaction interface uses network security to encrypt data in transit and validate user sessions, while an e-commerce checkout securely transmits credit card details. Understanding these patterns is essential for creating features like secure API calls, protected user profiles, and compliance with data protection regulations in real-world products.
